provenance.author: block writer B5 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Central image (plan: the book's key picture): Arth alone draws the sword in the silent churchyard. The beat follows Malory's errand: Cai left his sword under a bench at the inn after showing it off; the inn is locked because everyone is at the tournament; Arth takes the stone's sword for Cai 'just for today', does not think of the prophecy, and is honestly surprised it is not stuck ('Mae pawb yn dweud bod y cleddyf yn sownd, ond dyw e ddim yn sownd!'). Cai recognises it (no gold on the hilt, cf. Pennod 8) and goes pale; the chapter ends on Arth's 'Wnes i ddim ei ddwyn e!' and Cai looking at his father, which hands 27 its opening.

Target: gwneud-past in all persons appears in dialogue (wnes i, wnest ti, wnaeth e, wnaethon ni, wnaethoch chi in Pensa/Gramadeg only, wnaethon nhw); narration stays in the -odd preterite, which gives the contrast the Gramadeg table states (Tynnodd Arth = Wnaeth Arth dynnu). Possessive-object bridge: ei roi e, ei ddangos e, ei dynnu e, ei weld e, ei ddwyn e; a'i in 'y cleddyf a'i lafn disglair' and 'a'i ddangos e'.

Continuity assumptions (21–25 written in parallel): checked against 21–23 on disk: the party lodges at the small inn by the church (23); Cai arms in the knights' tent at the tournament field by the walls; he left his sword under the inn bench the night before and the party left the inn early; Myrddin is missing and Dafi rides under Mali's cloak; Cai is due to fight Gwalchmai at ten on the second day; Dafi travels under Mali's cloak with Myrddin's watch and announces the hours; Elen (at the inn), Modlen and Pero (at the llys, 21) do not appear. If 25 places the sword elsewhere the first section needs a one-line adjustment only.
mor hawdd â chleddyf o wain uses the equative receptively (productive from 37), as 25 introduced it; it is not tested.
Open slot: neb (CorCenCC top 2000), declared in learning_contract.open_slot_ids and the delta; needed for the empty town and churchyard and for 'Wnaeth neb lwyddo'.
Delta adds forms: safodd (sefyll), brysia (imperative), and gwneud-past auxiliary forms with a 'past' card stage for gwneud.

Codex (gpt-6-astra) review applied: avoided 'dod â ti'n ôl' (standard â thi), corrected the llithro gloss, widened C2 answers. C8 keeps the course-wide formula 'A ti?' (the checker requires it); two Codex reviews flag standard 'A thi?' (a + AM): a course-wide decision for the integrator.

Full Codex Welsh review (docs/reviews/welsh-review-26-31-full-2026-10-18.md) applied; its verdicts on the writer's [?] questions are recorded as resolutions (all accepted, none deferred to a human beyond the general fluent sign-off). Applied: vocative 'Dafarnwr!' (s046), A8/A10/C2 answers widened, Gramadeg pair 'Lwyddodd neb. ↔ Wnaeth neb lwyddo.', ddofn gloss shows dwfn → dofn.

Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrences added. Cai's panic: gwaethaf + enillydd (s134, echoing the red lord's 'diwrnod gwaethaf' in 25) and taro twice (s135, 'Gyda llwy?'). Arth's run: adfail + amffitheatr (s037), milltir + gwastad (s136, the flat icy road that sets up his slip in s059), crwn (s041, the dog). Narration: cystadlu (s002; its last clause split off as s137 for length), dur (s077), mwy + sedd + cystadleuaeth + mwyaf (s105). Arth's 'Mae pawb yn dweud ei fod e'n anodd, ond roedd e'n hawdd!' (s129: anodd ↔ hawdd contrast pair). No gloss symbols to replace.
Recall pass revision 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/recall-pass-critique-2026-10-18.md): critique row s041 reverted (no round dog).

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19: glosses moved to first use (gafael s087 → s083; syndod s096 → s095, now 'rhyfeddu → syndod' instead of the bare '"O!"'); welw gloss no longer uses the untaught fel; late duplicate glosses removed (welw s121, ddwyn s131). primary_new_grammar.label: Colloquial gwneud-past in all persons: wnes i / wnest ti / wnaeth e / wnaethon ni / wnaethoch chi / wnaethon nhw + soft-mutated verbal noun (Wnes i gyfrif, Wnaeth neb lwyddo); negatives (Wnes i ddim …) and questions (Wnest ti …? — Do / Naddo); contrast with the inflected preterite (Tynnodd e / Wnes i ei dynnu e); bridge: pronoun object as possessive + verbal noun (ei ddwyn e, ei roi e, a'i)

introductions.how: context (doedd neb … : dim marchogion, dim milwyr, dim plant)

cover.alt: In a silent snowy churchyard, Arth stands alone at a big grey stone and draws a shining sword out of it with both hands; nobody else is there.
cover.art_brief: THE KEY IMAGE OF THE BOOK: give it the most care. A small snowy churchyard at Caerllion in clear, low winter morning light (match place-caerllion.png: Roman red-brick-banded wall behind, small stone church with a bell-turret and a little coloured glass window; Caerllion palette of red brick and snow). Snow on low graves and on two or three simple stone crosses; bare trees white with frost. In the centre, a large rough grey stone with a black iron anvil set on top of it, dusted with snow and old dust, faint unreadable carved marks on its side (no legible letters). Arth (11, slight build, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles, Cai's old brown wool coat, far too big for him, worn open over his oversized moss-green tunic and knotted brown belt, dark grey leggings, knee-high brown boots; snow on his hair and shoulders) stands on the stone's step, both hands on the plain, dull grey hilt, drawing the long straight sword up and out of the anvil in one easy movement; the blade catches the sunlight and shines, a little puff of stone-dust falling into the snow. His breath shows white; his face is surprised, not triumphant. He is completely alone: an empty path of his own footprints leads back to the open churchyard gate; one blackbird sits on a cross watching him. Silence, stillness, light. No crown, no other people. No text.

grammar.nodyn_en: Spoken southern Welsh often tells the past with gwneud: wnes i, wnest ti, wnaeth e, wnaethon ni/nhw, wnaethoch chi + a soft-mutated verb-noun (Wnes i gyfrif). Same meaning as -odd. Negative: Wnes i ddim … (no mutation after ddim). Answer Do / Naddo. A pronoun object goes before the verb-noun as a possessive: Wnes i ddim ei ddwyn e.
